subject: general
question:
Which of the following is a correct nomenclature of the given structure?

CH₃CH₂OH
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethan - 1 - ol**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **given structure is CH3CH2OH**.
 
• This** is a two-carbon chain with an -OH (alcohol) functional group.**
 
• A **one-carbon chain is named methane**.
 
• A **two-carbon chain is named ethane.**
 
• Since** there are two carbons, the base name is ethane. **
 
• The -OH group is on the first carbon (you start numbering from the end closest to the functional group).
 
• So, **the correct name is ethanol, or more formally, ethan-1-ol.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**The key to naming organic molecules is to:

 
• **Identify the longest carbon chain:** This gives you the base name (methane, ethane, propane, etc.).
 
• **Identify the functional group:** This determines the suffix (-ol for alcohols, -al for aldehydes, -one for ketones, etc.).
 
• **Number the chain:** Start numbering from the end closest to the functional group to give it the lowest possible number.
